scope.statement: A reaction is screened only if it is among openFDA's 999 most-reported reactions for all drugs and among the 999 most-reported with isotretinoin, with at least 3 reports with isotretinoin. The all-drugs list is full (999 reactions, the smallest with 9,059 reports), so reactions reported fewer times across all drugs are not screened. The isotretinoin list is full (999 reactions, the smallest with 13 reports), so reactions reported fewer times with isotretinoin are not screened. 636 reactions met all three conditions and were screened. Reports are counted whenever they name isotretinoin (generic name or active substance), whether or not it was the suspect drug. openFDA data last updated 2026-07-30.

legend.label_status: covered (named in warnings, adverse reactions, patient counselling or a leaflet's side effects, with the sections in label_sections), mentioned_outside_effect_text (named only where coverage doesn't count, with the sections), not_mentioned (the search doesn't find its name, a set synonym or a simple spelling change, though a broader term may still cover it), or no_label

openfda.note: Each read of a direct count's REST table fetches openFDA once, and registering a new one costs one more the first time. The drug's own list and the all-drugs list are the screen's tables, read from Zetaris's cache.

limits: Designated medical events are matched by exact name, and pregnancy, breastfeeding and newborn terms by whole words in the name, so a related term that uses none of those words is missed.
Missed serious terms come from the drug's own list, where the run's serious counts cover them. The serious flag is for the whole report, which may list other reactions.
41 terms outside the screen have no serious count (they are below the cutoff of the drug's serious-report list), so they could not be judged and are not listed.
18 terms outside the screen have 50% or fewer of their reports flagged serious, so they are not listed.
9 serious terms outside the screen are left out as non-clinical by the app's rules (administrative, social or pregnancy-exposure terms).

The drug's own list is full (999 terms, smallest count 13). Designated medical events missing from it were counted directly in openFDA, and pregnancy and newborn terms by an openFDA word search. Missed serious terms below its cutoff are not seen.
The word search came back as openFDA's largest list (999 terms, smallest count 1), so a pregnancy or newborn term with 1 or fewer reports may be missing.

dossier.analyst_summary: Pregnancy is not an adverse reaction caused by isotretinoin but a contraindicated condition; the high reporting rate is driven by iPLEDGE mandatory pregnancy reporting, so it does not warrant signal review. Depressed mood is a clinical event with a strong reporting signal (PRR 4.88) for isotretinoin. The label's warnings_and_cautions section covers it under depression and mood disturbance, so it is a known labeled risk and lower priority for further review.

read_by.code: every queue item is compared with the verdict the World Model holds from earlier runs (since_last_run), and a new label version reopens the verdicts that rested on the old one
read_by.agent_prompts: none: earlier verdicts are kept out of the Analyst's and Reviewer's prompts, because a past answer shown to the model is read as evidence (Nightshift's H-MEM replay, found 24 Oct)

untested_factors: Confounding by indication beyond the Analyst's judgement (no stratified counts yet)
Reporter type and country only for review-next items, as context flags. Copies of one case re-filed by many companies are not collapsed into patients
Co-reported drugs beyond the Skeptic's top co-drugs, items beyond its top review_next items, and interactions among three or more drugs. Adjustment is for one co-drug at a time
Every report naming the drug (generic name or active substance) is counted, whether or not it was the suspect drug

Only reactions in openFDA's 999 most-reported for all drugs and in the drug's own 999 most-reported are screened (sizes and cutoffs in data.scope), and only with 3 or more reports. The safety net lists designated medical events, pregnancy and newborn terms, and the unscreened terms with mostly serious reports, for a person to review, not as signals
dossier.caveat: FAERS reports show an association between a drug and a reported event, not that the drug caused it. Reports are voluntary, unverified and affected by reporting bias. This is not medical advice; openFDA asks that its data not be relied on for medical decisions.

q-cbdd09a9.sql:
SELECT reaction, a, b, c, d,
  ROUND((a / (a + b)) / (c / (c + d)), 2) AS prr,
  ROUND((a + b + c + d) * POWER(GREATEST(ABS(a * d - b * c) - (a + b + c + d) / 2, 0), 2)
        / ((a + b) * (c + d) * (a + c) * (b + d)), 1) AS chi2
FROM (
  SELECT dr.reaction,
    CAST(dr.reports AS DOUBLE) AS a,
    CAST(dt.total - dr.reports AS DOUBLE) AS b,
    CAST(rt.reports - dr.reports AS DOUBLE) AS c,
    CAST(gt.total - dt.total - rt.reports + dr.reports AS DOUBLE) AS d
  FROM openfda.faers_d2_isotretinoin_reactions dr
  JOIN openfda.faers_reaction_totals rt ON rt.reaction = dr.reaction
  CROSS JOIN (SELECT SUM(reports) AS total FROM openfda.faers_d2_isotretinoin_total) dt
  CROSS JOIN (SELECT SUM(reports) AS total FROM openfda.faers_total) gt
  WHERE dr.reports >= 3
) t
WHERE c > 0
ORDER BY prr DESC

agents.name: Data Clerk
agents.role: Registers openFDA FAERS counts and the current label in Zetaris and computes the disproportionality screen there

agents.name: Analyst
agents.role: Classifies each strong reaction against the label and revises when the Reviewer objects

agents.name: Reviewer
agents.role: Re-checks every finding's numbers and label quote in code, then accepts, rejects with an objection, or leaves the dispute unresolved

agents.name: Skeptic
agents.role: Tests the strongest review-next findings against co-reported drugs and sends challenged ones back for review

models.note: the model that served each call is in the trace (llm_call events, served_by)
